Definition: a feeding upon, i.e. grasping after
BiblicalUsage: The Preacher looked on all the works done under the sun and called them vanity and grasping after wind. He surveyed the works of his own hands and found them the same, and he hated life because the work done under the sun was grievous to him. Even labour itself, done for a neighbour's envy, is vanity and grasping after wind.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word names the hunger at the heart of every life lived without God. We grasp at wind because we were made to hold something solid, and only God is solid enough to hold. The Preacher's verdict stands until a man turns from the wind to the One who made it.
